question: Can the frozen eight partially supported functions supply nontrivial closed local syntax, and repeated lexical-candidate uses, without extending the frontend?
identities: Use exactly the eight source IDs and hashes in the prototype protocol and final manifest; do not replace any input.
selection: Within body descendants, closed roots of kind call, method_call, binary, unary, assign, reference, field, index, tuple, array, return, block_expression or let, with at least three descendant nodes including root. Keep only maximal eligible subtrees (no eligible ancestor). Threshold is a descriptive nontriviality rule, not a retrieval score.
measurements: All eight per-unit counts, including zero
Selected root IDs/ranges and node counts
Repeated same-binder candidate groups (two or more local-use occurrences), not raw name groups
Unknown local-use presence reported separately from syntax closure
limits: No rerun of exporter, no syntax expansion, no models, ranking, code changes or new source selection. A closed subtree is only closed under exported subset. Binding candidates remain unresolved by compiler. Missing ancestors and opaque interiors cannot be inferred.
decision: If no useful repeated-use structure is observed, do not claim readiness for a variable-use feature comparison; distinguish syntax-only opportunity from binding evidence. Do not tune the threshold to obtain a positive result.
stop: One deterministic census, repeat equality check, independent steering decision. Retain unfavorable outcomes.
